statements.text: This week, I introduced the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act. This legislation would bring transparency and accountability to AI-driven layoffs as artificial intelligence reshapes the American workforce at an unprecedented pace. AI has the potential to uplift workers, but right now, too many companies are using it as coverup to push workers out.

AI should lift workers up, not become an excuse to push them out. I introduced the AI-Related Jobs Impacts Clarity Act to require large companies and federal agencies to report AI-driven layoffs to the Department of Labor. Innovation and accountability must go hand in hand. If AI is changing jobs, wages, and local economies, workers and policymakers deserve the truth. Nevadans deserve a future where technology creates opportunity, protects workers, and respects the people who built these companies. #NV04

AI is the economic revolution for our generation, and Black Americans cannot be left behind. Innovation cannot come at the expense of workers’ privacy. @SenWarren and I are leading 119 of our colleagues from both parties and both chambers of Congress in urging Spirit Airlines and Google to protect workers’ sensitive personal information from identification, profiling, and misuse. Nearly 1,000 former Spirit Airlines employees in Nevada could be impacted. Their personal information should not be sold to train AI without strong, enforceable safeguards in place. Read my full statement here: https://t.co/9lhoutbtbI

“Spirit’s workers handed over this information because their jobs required it, not so it could be sold to train a different company’s AI,” said Rep. Horsford. “In Las Vegas alone, nearly 1,000 people were laid off from Spirit. They should not have to worry about their payroll records, disciplinary files, and private messages being used by a company they never worked for. Innovation cannot come at the expense of workers’ privacy, and no employee data should move until real, enforceable safeguards are in place.”
statements.venue: Press release on letter to Spirit Airlines and Google on employee data for AI training

The price you see should be the price you pay. Period. Hidden fees, subscription traps, and AI-powered pricing tools are changing how Americans pay for everyday necessities.
